meaning: The unit a .phyre asset file is read in: the loader reads one cluster after another until the file ends. A cluster is read front to back: header, packed namespace, instance lists and their data, fixup tables, then D3D11 data.
A resource container whose first dword is @FRP, with a version (0 or 1), a section count and an offset table that leads to its child sections.

The 16 rows of 32-bit masks at 0x0215F1C0 that keep menus and buttons shut during scenes, movies and battle moments. Each row belongs to one part of the game, and a set bit in any row blocks that bit's actions.
also_called: action policy; action-policy row; availability bit

meaning: The moment a character or enemy locks in an action, from the menu, a gambit, its AI, an automatic attack or the next hit of a combo. The commit 0x0030F760 stores the action data, target handle and action id on the unit; nothing about damage, cost or timing is decided then.

The id of what a battle unit does, stored at unit +0x714 by the commit 0x0030F760. An id up to 0x21E clears the unit's target list and appends the target; an id from 0x4000 to 0x4166 is accepted and leaves the list alone; any other id makes the commit return 0.

The step a committed action has reached in the per-unit state machine 0x00304850, kept in unit byte +0x6B4. The 13 phases (0 to 12) run the delay, setup, approach and charge, arrival, the wait to be shown, execution (targets gathered, results worked out, effects or the scene played) and the end; phase 12 returns 1, the action is finished.

The 60-byte row that defines one battle action: Attack, each magick and technick, item use, summon, Quickening, Concurrence, Foecraft move and trap. The rows are the 543-row st2e table in section 14 of battle_pack.bin, and the row holds the action's cost, charge, reach, targeting, area, power, element, statuses and text ids.

Bits 5-7 of an actor record's byte +0x03, which decide what code accepts the actor: class 3 is a steerable character the movement code moves, classes 1 and 3 have a readable position, and class 2 is a trigger line the setline verb gives six coordinates. Bits 0-3 of byte +0x0E are a separate nibble (0x00263C20).

The 32-bit number that names an actor record from outside its manager: the low word is the record's index in its manager, bits 16-19 the manager slot and bits 20-30 the record's discriminator. 0x003589B0 makes it and 0x003588B0 turns it back into the record, returning null when any part no longer matches.

One of five managers that own everything that moves or talks in a field. The first owns the field itself (townspeople, doors, pots, triggers, the party and the music); the others hold the actors a cutscene or event brings in, so a scene can load its own cast without touching the field's.

Section 12 of a zone or event script: the table of models (characters, monsters, treasure chests, gadgets, weapons) that a script's bind verbs usually name by position, so the table decides which body, chest or prop appears.

The record behind every actor in a field: every townsperson, door, trigger line, party member and monster is one record owned by one of the five actor managers. The records are carved out of one block when a field or scene loads and stay alive until the manager unloads.
The three-byte record navimapdata.bin keeps for every area id, read through seven accessors: the town flag, the MP regime, the Map entry, the area-name flag, the hold flag and the default leader.

One of the fifteen large memory regions (ids 0 to 14) that loaded models, effects and tables live in. Each has a page map, an optional table of handle slots and a block heap, and the game compacts it as it goes, moving blocks to close gaps.

A named shared picture, such as buttonicon or battle_4_c, that menu sprites are cut from. A sprite is named by its atlas, a set, a group within the set and a frame within the group; the records sit in the eXt block of the atlas's picture.
The one 0x40-byte object at 0x01FD36A0 through which every sound effect, music track, battle voice and spoken line is loaded and played; it holds one controller per bank family.

A passive ability from the License Board or from gear, such as the +30 HP license (augment 74) or the extra Steal rolls of Thief's Cuffs. A unit's augment set is rebuilt from scratch when gear or licenses change; enemies get theirs from their own script.

A loaded table the battle system looks numbers up in, reached through one of the 64 qword registry slots 0x02EBF008 to 0x02EBF200. Most hold battle_pack.bin tables, five are rebound from the area's .ard and twelve hold license boards; a missing table makes the lookup read address 0.

A status a unit has for as long as its source stays: the stats rebuild ORs the character row's word +0x48 and each equipped item's word +0x08 into stats word +0x3C. Beside it, word +0x38 holds the statuses the unit cannot get (its immunities).

A sixteen-bit reference to one word-bank row: the bank in bits 11 to 15 and the row in bits 0 to 10. The checked reader returns 0 when either is past its count, but many readers index the banks inline with no bounds test.

An internal order id from 0x4000 to 0x4166, with no target list, that AI order lists and scripts use for moving, waiting, changing statuses and augment bits and adjusting stats. Each comes with a small order record whose i16 at +0x02 is the order's parameter; there are 359 order ids.

The 0xF50-byte combat record held by everything that can take part in a battle: the party, guests and every enemy on the field. There are thirty-two units; when all are taken, the next thing that would join a fight gets no unit, with no message and no error.

The one 31 GB file FFXII_TZA.vbf that holds the game's data. Only its index is read and checked at start-up; the data is read a piece at a time as the game needs it, and an index the game does not accept leaves the archive unmounted.

One of the 128 entries of 0x40 bytes in the script name-binding table, each holding a model a script has bound by its bound id. Every entry is on one of four lists (free, requested, live, retired), carries holder bits and a reference count, and has a stamp that its handle is checked against.

The number that names one binding entry: the entry's stamp in the high bits, its slot in the low bits and bit 15 set. It resolves only while the stamp matches, so a stale handle gives null rather than another model.

One piece of an arena, used or free: a 0x40-byte header (magic 0xFF12, the arena, the size, a tag word and links) followed by the payload. A block whose header has been overwritten makes the game write a memory dump and quit.
The 32-bit number a script names a model by: a letter class in bits 16 to 23 and a number in bits 0 to 15. A script argument above 0xFFFFFF is first looked up in the script image's name table.
The sixteen-bit operand of a call opcode that names the verb to run: its top four bits are the family, which picks a command table, and its low twelve bits the command in that table.
One of eight 0x110-byte records at 0x02097300 that each hold a camera view. The highest set bit of 0x02098DEC picks the record whose view is published, so a higher record outranks the ones below it.
A level 0 to 3 that the kill chain also has; it is what improves drops, and it rises when enough kills have been added since the last rise.

The per-character draw object that turns what the render record decides into draw calls. It holds the character's shader parameters (six lights and ambient, fog colour, refraction, shadow settings, bone matrices, PS2-style z-bias and projection matrices) and draws nothing until its setup ends.

One of 48 kinds in the selector table 0x01F000A0 that a presentation command of class 0x0B asks for a choice, and then plays the table entry of that choice. The listed kinds' handlers read the stream's render record, for example the locomotion selector or a random draw; every kind not listed returns 0.

The 0x100-byte Phyre::PClassDescriptor each reflected PhyreEngine class has, holding its name, instance size, alignment, namespace and parent; the loader finds each class of a .phyre file by name and matches its fields to the registered members.

The 0x130-byte body a steerable actor carries so that overlapping characters are pushed apart. 128 bodies sit in one pool at 0x02B4E4C0; a body is attached through the actor's secondary context, and the 129th actor gets none and drops out of the separation pass.

The 32 MB block at 0x01F7F4C0 that Gi commands are carved from. A request takes (size & ~0xF) + 0x10 bytes, the cursor restarts at the base when the request would not fit below the end, commands are never freed one by one, and the frame-end reset rewinds the cursor to its mark.
A number that names one physical input, held as a button code in an input record: 1-3 the mouse buttons, 11-27 any of up to 18 pads, 28-152 the keyboard. A code in no band is never polled.
One of the six fixed points in the frame at which effects are drawn, so some effects sit behind characters and others in front of the menu; the frame draw asks for effects once per layer.
The list at [0x02F8F2F8] that blended effect primitives are filed on instead of drawing at once: 0x28-byte entries with a sort key, 40,960 at most, sorted and drained by 0x003A3740.

A verb whose command record has a begin or a poll callback. Only those with a poll can hold the issuing script across frames, and only while the poll returns odd; the wait slot's scratch block carries the verb's state between frames. A verb with neither callback is instantaneous and completes inside the call.

The .ebp file every zone and every event has: the magic EBP2 and a twenty-slot section table that says which parts (script image, script text, camera tables, lighting, position entries and others) it carries and where each starts.

One piece of a running effect (a spark, streak, sprite, ring, mesh or light). Elements are born in bursts by their emitter, move and change colour as their authored tracks say, can spawn further pieces, and disappear when their lifetime runs out or they leave their visibility window.
The top level of a running effect: a 0x3B0-byte record made from a template, with its kind in byte +0, a list of emitters and a block of sixteen timeline players.

The chunk stream every spell, summon, Quickening, hit flash, event effect and map effect is built from. An .efx file is one stream; streams also sit in .efb map banks, in the @FEF section of .cm models and in .mpk map packs.

One of 32 records made when a render source is an @FRP container with an @FEF section; it owns the effect context built for that data. Its id holds the slot, a 22-bit counter and 3 in the top bits, so a recycled slot gets a new id.

The middle level of a running effect: it belongs to an effect instance, carries an 0x800 emitter record and an 0xA00 element definition, and fires at intervals its authored tracks set, birthing elements. An element can start a child emitter.

The sixteen-bit id behind items, equipment, loot, magicks, technicks, gambit conditions, key items, reward packages, package selectors, Quickenings, bazaar goods and gil amounts: the top nibble picks the inventory class and the low twelve bits are the index inside it.

One 88-byte row of directory slot 2 of an area's .ard file, bound to registry slot 0x02EBF120 when the area loads. It holds the enemy's class row, name word, model scale and the other fields the installer 0x0023A570 applies to a unit; the shipped area files hold 1,146 of them.

A numbered group a zone script puts enemies in (verb btlAtelSetEventFlagGroup). The group table keeps a member mask and a dead mask per group, and when every member has died the party is locked and the group's number is handed to the zone script.

An enemy's hidden memory of how much each party member has bothered it: one byte per party-table row id 0-39, from +0x1A of the enemy's spawn record, with a decay timer at +0x19. Actions raise it, it decays while the enemy is not engaged, and AI orders can pick the most hated member.

The 52-byte data row of one weapon, shield, armor, accessory or ammunition, in section 13 of battle_pack.bin. Row n is equipment id 0x1000 + n; it holds the price, attack or defense, element, statuses and the offset of its bonus record.
The R2 toggle that makes the party run instead of fighting; it takes about a second to engage. It is held in the force-fight flag 0x01E0C2B8, which is cleared while Escape Mode is on.

Two working-memory heaps a field gets when its actors are bound: heap 13 EVTMEM (1 MiB) and heap 14 SMNMEM (100 KiB), for the actors of events and summons. A field on the list, or a town, loads those actors from the general pool instead.
The .ebp script of an event, loaded into one of actor managers 1 to 3; its files are the .ebp, .mot, .snd and .vpc at the event's path index.

One of the ten eight-byte opacity values a render record carries at +0x4C0. A channel ramps from a base towards a target over a number of frames, and what is drawn is a product of several channels, so separate fades never fight.

State 2 of the main state machine (0x0022A770), the frame the game runs in the field: after the pad and the draw set-up it runs, when 0x0017E4E0() is 0, a number of passes (0x001EC760()), each running zero or more simulation steps and ending in the camera, the end-of-frame list and the pacer.

The one integer that names a map: the first argument of mapjump, kept at save payload +0x1044, and the index into the archive file table (three paths per id: .ebp, .mot and .fpk), the MapRef resource and the music table.

The RAM cache of files the game has read before. When the cache route applies (0x01F83440 set, a non-zero selector, a cacheable open and a name that passes the filter), the name is turned into an upper-case key, hashed and looked up there before the archive is tried.

One of the 64 request slots of 0x80 bytes in which a file load waits in the read queue. When more than 64 loads are outstanding, the code asking for the next one stops and services the queue until a slot frees.

The per-language .fst file (twelve ship in FileSizeTables, each 820,000 bytes with no header) that gives the size of every file by resource kind and id, 0xFFFFFFFF meaning no file. Every file loaded by kind and number is sized from it first.
One entry of the 202-pointer function table at 0x01EFA5C0, called as slot(source, target, &context). Every number a battle action produces comes from these slots; a recipe names slots by their index.

The target condition of a gambit line: one of the 256 32-byte rows of battle_pack.bin section 7, bound to 0x02EBF0D8, with the id 0x6000 + row. Its menu name comes from a row word naming a text entry, and its help line (text id 16000 + row) is entry row of listhelp_targetchip.bin; row 255 has no help id.

One line of a character's gambit list, holding a target condition and an action. The list is tried from the top, and the first line whose condition finds a target and whose action can be carried out is the one that runs; a line switched off or missing its condition or action is not in the list.
One of the three gambit lists each character has; all three start as copies of the character's preset, and the menu chooses which one is used.

The main gameplay generator, a standard MT19937 with its state at 0x02EB3870. Hits, misses, damage spread, status chances and chest contents come from it, and it is reseeded from the clock every time a save is loaded.

A set of functions whose bodies are the same instruction sequence and differ only in constants, offsets and call targets, such as deleting destructors, atexit-registered static initialisers and vtable installs.

One of the small Gi* command objects (eighteen classes) that draw scene brackets, sprites, coloured rectangles, screen images, primitives and PS2-style effect packets. The game thread creates them each frame; PhyreEngine's render thread runs each against the D3D11 primitive renderer.

The PS2 Graphics Synthesizer register settings the remaster still builds every frame: 0x0036D400 composes FRAME_1 and ZBUF_1 from the 512 by 448 PS2 frame and writes them into the current GS command buffer.
A party member whose selector is 7 to 25, as opposed to the main characters 0 to 6. A guest travels with the party for a while, and a guest's gear is never added to the inventory.

The one 0x10FD0-byte HUD object, pointed to by 0x0209BE80, that the party HP and MP list, the battle menu, the help line and the gauges hang off. It owns a 0x8030-byte pool and draws the target lines, the target ring and the selection marker.

One of the fifteen classes (5 to 19) an encoded id's top nibble picks, the class being the nibble plus five. Each has a 0x58-byte descriptor giving up to three regions of the battle state block that hold its counts or bits (none for some classes), its id count and its mutate and query handlers.
A function body that is exactly one jmp rel32 into .text, so one body is reached under two addresses; the image has 763 of them.
The count of kills of the same kind of enemy in a row, where the same kind means the same enemy class byte; killing a different class breaks it. The number shown stops at 999.

Byte +0x05 of a stats record: 0 for a unit built from the party table, 1 for one built from the area's enemy table. It is the high byte of the definition id the installer applies, so every piece of combat code can tell party and enemy units apart by it.
The two-letter code (jp, en, fr, de, it, es, kr, ch, cn, or none) that the Language setting indexes; the choice decides which data folder the text, voices and fonts load from.

One of the twelve job boards, the files board_1.bin to board_12.bin: a 24-by-24 grid of squares the character buys one at a time. Some squares, such as the Espers and Second Board, are on every board.

A record of the license node table 0x02EBF038, 361 rows in the shipped battle_pack.bin: its name word, its type label, its LP cost, its category (which gives the requirement kind), its refusal rule, the party rows that start owning it and the ids the square grants.
also_called: License Board node; node; licence node

meaning: The object that appears where an enemy with a successful loot roll died; the party collects everything in it, up to seven stacks, by walking the controlled character over it. It waits one minute, and only ten can exist at once.
The one-slot store at 0x0215F1A0 that holds a menu request (pending and blocked bytes, the id and a parameter) until it is delivered; a second post before delivery overwrites the first.
The 16-bit word at the start of the save payload (script variable class 0, offset 0) that marks how far the story has come; scripts write it, most of the writes being in a zone's director actor.

The 0x288-byte block that holds one actor manager. Five sit in an array at 0x02098E10, so slot n is at 0x02098E10 + n * 0x288; a script file is bound to a slot and the slot's record pool holds its actors.

A map's .efb file: an effect stream plus a table saying which of its effects to start. The field loader asks for one per map, reads it into a fixed block tagged EffMapNo and publishes it at 0x02ADD088; only the map teardown frees it.
The low byte of a party seat: the row of the party table and of the forty member records that names one party member. 0xFF is an empty seat.

One of a model's motion files, which follow its .cm in a fixed order: a character has 24 lanes, of which lanes 0-15 are its animation sets, and a monster has 10. A battle unit's lane is the animation set its main-hand weapon's motion class picks.

The 0x230-byte region of an actor record at +0x120, reached through the pointer at +0xB8, present for every sequence but 0. Its first three floats are the actor's world position, and it holds the steering request the field runtime reads.

The number every field character carries (actor i16 +0x102) that picks a pair of names from npcdic.bin; the persistent flag with the same number decides which of the two is shown. A negative name id makes the actor show its own literal text.

The engine side of a verb: a 32-byte record in one of the five command tables holding a begin, a poll and a result callback (and an unused null slot). The call runs them as one fall-through: begin on the first visit, then the poll, then the result, which pushes one value.

The flat mesh of regions joined by portals that an area carries, slot four of the area's map pack. Units search it for a route and walk from portal to portal; some portals are doors a zone script opens and closes per kind of mover, and height plays no part.

A list of orders a unit tries top to bottom, split into subgroups (phases). Every unit carries four order-set pointers, tried in a fixed order: the re-plan set, the issued command's set, the unit's own list and the default set; an enemy's own lists come from its area file.

The per-frame list of render job objects (opaque characters and maps, ambient occlusion, water, post-processing and the rest) that the frame creates, files and runs later in the order they were appended. Walks filter it with a class-key mask; nothing sorts it.
A record's position in its actor manager's record pool, from 0 to the pool's count - 1; 0x00358940(slot, ordinal) returns the record pointer, or null past the count.
A row of the 256-row selector table (battle_pack.bin directory entry +0x9C): id 0xA000 + n, inventory class 15, whose six ids in two triples name the reward packages it chooses between.

The 0x7410-byte block inside the save image that 0x02EBF190 points at. It holds the forty member stats records, the inventory counts and learned bits, the seats, leader and battle mode, the mode flags, three formulas' counters and the gambit banks.
The member the player controls, whom the others follow in a formation. The engine keeps the leader as one actor handle at 0x022C7FE0; the party block keeps the leader's selector at +0x5AA4.
One of the nine two-byte entries of a slot map. Seats 0-3 are the active members and seats 4-8 the reserve; the low byte of a seat is the member's selector, and 0xFF is an empty seat.

The authored 40-row table of the main characters, guests, the Chocobo and the Espers, reached through registry slot 0x02EBF130 (battle_pack.bin directory entry +0x44). Row n belongs to the stats record whose type byte +0x04 is n.

PhyreEngine's container for an object placed in a scene: it holds its first component, its world matrix and a node of the world-matrix registry. Each PComponent holds the next component, its entity and its own class descriptor.

A yes-or-no flag kept in the save payload, one bit per id, in one of the five banks: Primary (map-jump groups and map icons), Bank2048 (names learned by talking), Bank512 (chests opened and traps fired in its first half, scripts only in its second), Bank64A and Bank64B (scripts only).

A per-area container (.mot, .snd, .vpc, .vpcjp) that holds an area's extra motions, its sound set or its voice clips: a PKFL tag and a directory of offset and size pairs (16 or 64 slots) so a script can ask for a slot by number. Only the directory is held in memory; each payload is read on its own.

The 0x3A0-byte entry that plays a character's authored motion stream: it picks the track to play, such as the gait the locomotion selector chooses, and advances it every frame. Entries are reached by id through the reference container at root +0x160.

The fields each quest q (0 to 255) keeps in the save payload: an ordered bit, a cleared bit, a scenario byte, a contract word set to the field id when the quest is first ordered, and an OK bit, plus the total of quests cleared.
One of the 18 ids 0xC000-0xC011 of the 32-row Quickening and Esper table (inventory class 17), owned as one bit and named by word +0x22 of Quickening actions 208-225.
The pending list of file requests that the pump works through from its head, keeping on while the head changes; a state that has to wait ends the pass.

One of 109 lists of calculator slots an action resolves through: a first list that decides hit, evade, block, parry and knockback, and a committed list run by 0x00385F60. An action takes its recipe from byte +0x08 of its row; recipe 0 means the weapon's.

The non-zero code the availability check 0x002FFCF0(actionId, unit) returns when an action cannot be used; 0 means available. The battle menu, gambits, enemy AI and the running action all ask the same check.
A 0x260-byte entry of the render root's +0xDA0 bank, one of 160 slots; a render record names its instance at +0x64.

The record a character model is drawn from, which keeps its look between frames: the motion event it plays, how faded it is, its shadows and its colour. There are 160, allocated once at start-up, and a new record waits one update on a pending list before it is drawn.

The bank of 0x50-byte entries at manager + 0xD90 that every loaded source that renders passes through. An entry keeps its source either as an owned copy (mode 0) or as a retained handle (mode 1), and a second request for the same tag and name returns the existing entry.

A row in a bank owned by a table descriptor, through which a loaded resource is reached. Its mode word at +0x04 decides how its base is found: mode 0 decodes the inline handle at +0x18, mode 1 decodes the handle at +0x30 into +0x38 while 0x02B62E10 is set and otherwise returns +0x38 as cached, and any other mode gives 0.
One of the 41 path arrays the game names its files by. A file is requested and sized by a kind and an id, the id being the file's position in the kind's array.
A row of the 512-row reward-package table (battle_pack.bin directory entry +0x98). Row n is package id 0x9000 + n, inventory class 14; giving the id gives the package's gil and items together.
The on-disk form of a save: a 12-byte header (magic SAFH, the decoded image size and a key rotation 0-31) followed by the image, compressed with zlib and encrypted with RC4.
The decoded save, 0x56690 (353,936) bytes: a 512-byte header followed by the persistent payload. The game keeps it in memory while playing and copies it when saving.
The 0x56490-byte persistent part of the save image after its 0x200-byte header; 0x002EF2B0 returns its address, and save offsets are given relative to it.

One save file, named FFXII_ plus the slot number as three digits, in the save directory. The game also writes a hidden autosave to slot 0 when an area changes, except for the area changes a shipped list names.
Slot 0 of a class with a virtual destructor: it destroys the object, frees it when bit 0x1 of its flag argument is set, and returns the object.
A numbered set of save data (party, levels, gear, gambits, licenses, gil and items) that a script asks for with verb 0x302B btlAtelSetNextSetSaveData; the next area start applies it once.

One of seven independent layers (0-6) a screen fade to black, white or a colour runs on. Each is a 0x30-byte fade record holding the handle of the screen effect that draws it, a state, the direction and an effect descriptor; fades on different layers run at the same time.

One of 80 records (five area slots of sixteen) through which the motionread, motionreadsync and motiondispose verbs load, wait for and free a script's animation sets; each record moves through the states idle, armed, held, read in flight, registered and dispose requested while in flight.

A request, filed by a script or by the engine, for an actor to run one of its functions. The actor keeps a short list of request entries, ranks them by channel (six or eight channels, by actor type), runs the most urgent and tells the requester when it has started or finished.

The second gameplay generator, one 32-bit word at 0x022C256C that every draw steps three times. Loot drops, the chain coin, where enemies appear and which action an AI picks come from it; it is reseeded from a counter each time an area is entered.

A render record's entry in the skeleton bank. It knows its own index, the skeleton it hangs from and an entry attached to it, and the bank keeps an update list in which a parent always comes before its children. A held sword or shield stays in the hand because its bones are tied to the hand's bone.

One of five copies of the nine party seats kept in the battle state block at [0x02EBF190], 0x12 bytes apart, each read by a different part of the game: map 0 the live party, map 1 the fight, map 2 the battle command menu, map 3 the rest of the game, map 4 the members' field actors and the chocobo mount.

A bank file under ps2data/sound that holds sound effects, battle voices or a music track; the game ships no loose sound files. The families are block banks, six-digit banks, battle-voice banks and music banks, each opened by its own audio-manager controller.
The number a game request names a sound by: the block registry slot shifted left by 9 plus the sound's slot in the bank. An index file has 128 slots, so slots 128-511 of each id range name nothing.
The game's handle on one sound-driver Sound, kept in its bank's sound list and taken from and returned to a pool as sounds start and finish.

The 0x250-byte record every enemy placed by a zone script owns in the live keep bank (64 records). It outlives the battle unit and carries the enemy's death history, position and facing, persistence key, threat table and whole stats record, so a banked enemy comes back with its HP, statuses and grudges.
A cell of a License Board's 24-by-24 grid. It holds a license node number, and 0xFFFF means no square.

A battle unit's combat stats record, reached through unit +0x698. A party member's record sits in the battle state block at [0x02EBF190] + 8 + k * 0x1C8; an enemy's is the stats page of its spawn record. Byte +0x05 says which kind it is.

One of 32 status bits, status s being bit 1 << s, held in a stats record's words +0x64 and +0x3C, with immunities in +0x38. Each status has a 40-byte row in section 15 of battle_pack.bin that gives its duration, beat and flags.

One of the two 0x80-byte steering states inline in a movement context at +0x120 and +0x1A0. A move verb fills the current one. When a script takes the actor, the push copies slot 0 over slot 1 and hands slot 1 to the interruption clean; when it ends, the pop returns to slot 0 and replays the walk kept there, one level deep.
also_called: steering request; steering slot; steering state

meaning: One of the six homes (classes 0 to 5: global, file, local, msp, scratch1, scratch2) a script variable lives in, read by PUSHV and written by POPV. The class decides whether the value is kept in the save, lives only while the area's scripts are loaded, or sits in one of two shared 512-byte banks.

A sound-driver bank built from a buffer the game has filled with the start of a bank file, so long sounds such as spoken lines and music start before the whole file is in memory. A sound bank asks for one stream, a music bank for 2 to 16.

The list of units an action affects, held at unit +0x778 in the action context. When the action's state machine reaches its target step, the gatherer 0x0030D160 clears it, appends the chosen target first and gathers everyone else the action hits.
A control code inside a game string: one of the 14 control bytes 0x01-0x0E, or a 0x0F escape named by the selector character that follows it.

The number a menu or help string is looked up by. One form is group times 1000 plus row; the second takes the group as id / 10000 and searches the group's rows for a row whose own id equals the number. A row's id need not be group times 10000 plus row, so one string can answer to two numbers.

The registry of 28 stop requests that halts actors for menus, cutscenes, Stop magicks and skippable scenes. Each request has two permission records whose set bits exempt categories of actors (the party focus actor, the rest of the roster, other managed actors, the request's own actors); active requests stack, and every actor obeys the stricter.

Bit 15 of an area's navimapdata record. Inside a town the out-of-play rule for KO, Stone and X-Zone is waived, so a fallen member still walks, talks and shops with the party; entering a town also ends the kill chain.
The 8-byte flag word at the start of a battle unit (+0x000); bit 0 marks the slot in use, and the battle units page holds the table of its other bits.

The single static stack (0x02099AC0) through which script values, verb arguments and verb results pass: 64 slots, 63 usable, each tagged int or float. A pop from an empty stack gives 0, so a script that supplies too few arguments runs on zeros.
A native engine function that a zone script calls by a sixteen-bit number: the script pushes its arguments, names the verb and reads back one value.

One of 64 records, global to every script, that hold a cutscene's spoken lines: slot k always holds sub-file k of the calling event's voice pack, with both the .vpc and .vpcjp tables loaded and the language choosing which one is used.
The 0x28-byte record that each request channel of a script-bearing actor has; it holds the program counter and the wait state of whatever runs on that channel.

A menu element: every menu, window, list and gauge. It is built around a procedure that answers numbered messages, opens with a short slide or fade, answers input while it has the focus, and closes with the reverse animation.
A numbered message that a widget procedure answers or a sender raises; there are 56 ids, 1-26, 29-53 and 285-289.
One bank of the word block (entry +0xF8 of battle_pack.bin, word.bin) that holds the battle names; each row is two zero bytes followed by NUL-terminated strings.

Stop request 6 of the time-stop registry. Every conversation takes it when its script starts, so the rest of the world holds still while a talk or scene runs; it is released when its counter returns to 0.

Silicon Studio's bought-in post-effect library that makes the remaster's glare and depth of field; the game hands it each rendered frame and it writes the finished image. The EnableYebis key switches the whole pass off.
One map the area loader can enter, its context n, with its own zone script; 708 shipped zones, numbered 12 to 1,311, make up 215 areas.
The .ebp script of a zone, loaded into actor manager 0 when the zone is entered; its files are the .ebp, .mot and .fpk at the zone's path index.
